title: Microsoft PowerPoint Basics (Canada)
summary: By the end, learners can start a presentation with a theme, add slides and type in placeholders, insert a picture from their device, save their file, and start or leave a slide show.
goals: By the end, learners can start a presentation with a theme, add slides and type in placeholders, insert a picture from their device, save their file, and start or leave a slide show.
certificateNote: It is not a college diploma, degree, trade ticket, professional licence, or Microsoft Office Specialist certification.

lessons.title: What is PowerPoint, and how do you start?
lessons.html:
Microsoft PowerPoint is a program for slide shows. Microsoft’s basic-tasks guide says that to convey a message or a story, you break it down into slides. Think of each slide as a blank canvas for the pictures and words that help you tell your story.

When you open PowerPoint, you will see some built-in themes and templates. Microsoft says a theme is a slide design that contains matching colours, fonts, and special effects such as shadows and reflections.

To start with a theme (Microsoft’s Windows steps):

  1. On the File tab of the Ribbon, select New, and then choose a theme. PowerPoint shows a preview, with colour variations on the right.
  2. Click Create, or pick a colour variation and then click Create.

In PowerPoint for the web, Microsoft says you can select Browse templates to choose a theme.

People in Canada use slides for many everyday jobs: a short talk at a community hall, a volunteer orientation, or a simple update at work. This course uses Canadian spelling in the lesson text. On the screen, some buttons may still say “Color” because that is how the software is labelled.

This course is not a design diploma and not a MOS exam. If PowerPoint is not on the computer in front of you, ask your adult learning council which version they have. Do not buy software because this lesson mentioned it.

lessons.title: Add slides and type your words
lessons.html:
After the first slide, you add more slides for the rest of your story.

Microsoft’s steps:

  1. In the slide thumbnail pane on the left, select the slide that you want your new slide to follow.
  2. On the Home tab, select the lower half (or bottom half) of New Slide.
  3. From the menu, select the layout you want. The new slide is inserted.
  4. Click inside a placeholder and begin adding content.

A layout is the arrangement of boxes on the slide, such as a title box and a content box. Different layouts suit different slides: a title slide, a list of points, or a slide with a picture.

To add text, Microsoft says: select a text placeholder, and begin typing.

Keep the words short. Microsoft’s tips for an effective presentation say you want the audience to listen to you, instead of reading the screen. Use bullets or short sentences, and try to keep each item to one line. Microsoft also says to keep the number of slides to a minimum so the message stays clear.

A simple practise set (sample only): slide 1, “Saturday soup lunch”; slide 2, “Where and when”; slide 3, “How to help.” Type your own sample words. Do not put other people’s private information on a slide.

If the menus look a little different, look for New Slide on the Home tab and click a placeholder to type.

lessons.title: Add a picture
lessons.html:
A picture can help people remember your message. Microsoft says pictures and other visuals provide cues for the audience, but you should avoid putting too many visual aids on one slide.

To add a picture from your computer (Microsoft’s steps):

  1. On the Insert tab, select Pictures.
  2. Choose This Device (a picture saved on your computer or an internal server), browse for the picture, and choose Insert.

In PowerPoint for the web, after you insert the picture you can select it and drag to move it, and drag a corner handle to resize it. On Windows desktop, Microsoft also lists Stock Images (for Microsoft 365 subscribers) and Online Pictures. You do not need those extras for this lesson. Use a picture you have permission to use, such as a photo you took or a file your instructor gives you.

Do not copy a picture from a random website unless you know you may use it. This course is not copyright advice; when you are unsure, use your own photo or a file from class.

You can also add a simple shape. Microsoft’s steps: on the Insert tab, select Shapes, pick a shape, then click and drag on the slide to draw it. Then use the Shape Format (or Format) tab and the Shape Styles gallery if you want a colour or style.

One clear photo and a few words are enough for a community announcement slide.

lessons.title: Speaker notes and a clear look
lessons.html:
Slides work best when you do not cram in too much information. Microsoft says you can put helpful facts in speaker notes and refer to them as you present.

To add speaker notes on Windows:

  1. At the bottom of the window, click Notes.
  2. Click inside the Notes pane below the slide and type.

In PowerPoint for the web, Microsoft says to go to the View tab, select Notes, then click in the pane and type. You can drag the top border of the pane to make it larger.

Microsoft also offers these tips:

  • Choose an audience-friendly font size. Generally speaking, a font size smaller than 30 might be too difficult for the audience to see from a distance.
  • Apply a subtle, consistent theme so the background does not take attention away from your message. Built-in themes set contrast between a light background with dark text, or a dark background with light text.
  • Always check the spelling and grammar.

That font-size note is Microsoft’s general tip, not a law. Check how the slide looks from the back of the room if you can.

To change text colour or size in PowerPoint for the web, Microsoft says to select the text and use the Font options on the Home tab (including Font Color, Increase Font Size, Bold, Italic, and Underline). On Windows desktop, the basic-tasks page also describes Shape Format and WordArt tools. Look for the Home tab first.

Save as you go (Lesson 5) so you do not lose the notes you typed.

lessons.title: Save and show your slides
lessons.html:
Save often so you do not lose your work.

To save (Microsoft’s Windows steps):

  1. On the File tab, choose Save.
  2. Pick or browse to a folder.
  3. In the File name box, type a name, then choose Save.

Microsoft also says to press Ctrl+S often, or save the file to OneDrive and let AutoSave help. AutoSave is not a reason to skip saving yourself if you are working on a computer that does not use it. In PowerPoint for the web, Microsoft says work is saved automatically to OneDrive; you can click the file name in the title bar to rename it.

A clear name helps later, such as soup-lunch-slides or volunteer-orientation-practise.

To give your presentation:

  • On the Slide Show tab, click From Beginning to start at the first slide.
  • Click From Current Slide if you want to start from the slide you are on.

To move through the slides, Microsoft says you can click the mouse or press the spacebar. Arrow keys can also move forward and back. To leave Slide Show view at any time, press Esc. You return to the editing view.

This course does not require presenting online or broadcasting to a remote audience. Practise once with Esc so you know how to leave full screen.

Finishing this course does not make you a MOS-certified presenter.
